SK7074 Review a goto to a label

A goto names a label, so control leaves the statement nesting. goto case and goto default are not reported.

CategoryMaintainability
Default severitywarning
ScopeSyntax
Needs a compilationno
Runs under --load=looseyes
Cached per fileyes
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since1.3
SupersedesS907

Why

⚠ The position, because goto is legal and occasionally right. goto case and goto default are the only way C# expresses switch fall-through, they cannot leave the switch they are written in, and the flow they describe is already in front of the reader — reporting them would make this a style opinion about switch and get the whole rule turned off. A goto to a label is the other thing: its target is anywhere in the enclosing member, so what runs next can no longer be read off the nesting. Neither can it be computed: SK7001 and SK7002 derive complexity from the structure of the statements, and a label jump is an edge those numbers do not contain, which is why the rule sits in the same range as the metrics it distorts.

Example

Instead of:

foreach (var row in rows) {
    foreach (var cell in row) {
        if (cell.Bad) { goto broken; }
    }
}
broken:

Write:

// Extract the search, return early, or use a flag — whichever says what the loop means.

When it does not fire

⚠ Report-only, and this is one of the two rules the catalogue's shipping bar allows no fix for. Breaking out of nested loops is a real use with no mechanical rewrite: a flag, an extracted method and an early return are all correct and choosing between them is a design decision about what the loop means, so an edit that guessed would be worse than the goto. Every goto to a label is reported, including one inside a switch section, because the label is not confined to the switch. goto case and goto default are never reported. Generated code is excluded, which is where nearly all remaining goto lives — parser and state-machine generators emit it by design.
